messages:
ACME Integrations: Hey team — our March invoice shows ~14M embedding units but our dashboard shows ~4.6M. Can you help reconcile?
Ana: Sorry about that — can you paste a short sample of requests and the timeframe? Also your org ID?
ACME Integrations: org_98765. Sample rows from our client logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z POST /v1/embeddings {model: 'redwood-embed-1', inputs: 128, request_id: null} 200
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z POST /v1/rerank {model: 'rerank-lite', inputs: 128, pairwise: true, request_id: null} 200
```
ACME Integrations: We batch at 128 in the client and sometimes drop request_id because older clients didn’t set it.
Mike: Thanks — that already smells like duplicate/retry accounting. Dashboard groups by request_id when present, invoice billing runs off raw ingress events (we dedupe only when request_id is set).
Chris: quick check from backend logs for org_98765 around that time — I see repeated retries from the load balancer: 3 near-identical POSTs for the same batch window. The rerank endpoint emits pairwise counts: when pairwise=true we bill per pair (n*(n-1)/2). For n=128 that’s 8128 pairs per request which multiplies quickly.
Emma: If the dashboard deduped by request_id but the client wasn’t sending it, duplicates wouldn’t be visible in UI aggregates. Also the embedding pipeline has an internal sampler that collapses identical vectors when computing active cardinality for the UI metric — that’s not applied to billing.
ACME Integrations: So are we billed for retries plus pairwise expansion? That seems to match the ~3x gap.
Raj: Looks like in this case: 1) clients missing request_id -> retries counted multiple times, 2) rerank expands to pairs, 3) dashboard had a post-aggregation that collapsed exact-vector duplicates (mostly in ACME’s corpus) so the UI number is lower.
Ana: Can you run a repro so we can issue a credit? If you can share one batch payload (anonymized) we’ll run it on staging to show the delta.
ACME Integrations: Pasted one anonymized batch here: 
```json
{ "inputs": ["long-text-1", "long-text-2", "..."] , "metadata": {"customer_id":"acme-x"} }
```
ACME Integrations: We can also forward raw gzip logs for the window.
Chris: I ran the anonymized batch on staging with simulated 3 retries and pairwise=true. Results: dashboard-staging count (after UI dedupe): 1,024; billing-meter (raw events): 3 * 8,128 = 24,384 pairwise units. Attached shell I ran: 
```bash
# repro: simulate three client submits without request_id
for i in 1 2 3; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' \
    -d '{"model":"rerank-lite","inputs":[...],"pairwise":true}'
done
```
Mike: Given that, we should issue a one-time credit for the duplicate ingress caused by retries where request_id was missing. Also will flag docs to remind clients to set X-Request-ID and we’ll add a last-resort dedupe in billing for repeated identical payloads across short windows.
Ana: ACME — we’ll process a refund of the overcharged amount and keep you posted on the billing ticket. Sorry for the disruption.
ACME Integrations: Appreciate the quick investigation. Two asks: 1) can you add a dashboard view that shows pairwise-expanded accounting so we can sanity-check costs before invoicing, 2) can you provide a count breakdown for the March invoice per-endpoint (embeddings vs rerank pairwise)?
Emma: Yep — we can add a per-endpoint breakdown for the ingestion window and a pairwise-expanded column. I’ll add a low-latency report under Billing > Raw-ingress.
Raj: Follow-ups: (1) eng-ml will add server-side dedupe for retried payloads missing request_id within a 5s sliding window (patch PR #4821), (2) billing will add an optional dashboard toggle to show "expanded billing units" vs "UI-cardinality", (3) docs team to emphasize X-Request-ID.
metering-bot: Ticket created: BILL-3145 (refundable overcharge). Patch tracker: ENG-4821.
Ana: I’ve opened the support ticket and scheduled a sync with ACME for tomorrow 11am PT to walk the breakdown.
ACME Integrations: Thanks all — will join the call.
Chris: Post-mortem note — we should also check that long inputs truncated at the embed preprocessor aren’t leading to zero-dim vectors (we saw one case where truncation path returned an empty embedding and the UI pipeline filtered it out but billing still counted the call). Filing follow-up: ML-empties-443.
Ana: Closing loop for now, will update when refund posts and when the dashboard toggle is live.
